learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basic structure of a production company and can explain it.
They can name different organizations of enterprise and production systems and classify them into various systematizations.
They can name and describe the essential tasks of production organization.
They know the three main processes in a company: Design to Operate, Lead to Cash, and Plan to Produce (including associated processes) and can explain their interfaces in particular.
They know the different process patterns STO, ETO, CTO, CTO+, MTO, MTS, and ATO.

They are able to demonstrate how product structures and bills of material for production are created and how the information network, which must be provided for production in digitized companies, is to be implemented.
They know the tasks and methods of modern work preparation and can evaluate them.

Students can present the essential tasks and methods of production planning and control and their mapping in ERP systems against the backdrop of modern technologies such as Digital Design & Supply Chain Management, Industrial Data Science, AI, etc. Furthermore, students can derive the necessary measures for automated production monitoring.
Students can sketch and explain the necessary IT architectures for production.

Students use the content and possibilities of modern quality management by applying the learned methods and tools, enabling them to later assess and evaluate the relationships in the product life cycle regarding quality aspects.

They understand that preventive quality management is a crucial lever for a successful customer-supplier relationship by being able to successfully lead discussions and gain employees' commitment to later evaluate, initiate, and implement measures.

syllabus_topics: Production systematics & organization of production companies
Information systems in companies (ERP, PLM and MES)
Types, systematics, and modeling of product structures & bills of material
Process planning and work plan creation
Technological process chains (e.g., CAD-CAM-CNC process chain)
Production controlling & data acquisition in production
Quality management and its significance / context to synchronous production system / product-process-company quality
teaching_methods: Use of typical production software (e.g., SAP, MES systems)
